edges.description: Small-intestinal villous injury and epithelial-lineage loss produce the chronic diarrhea phenotype that defines AIE.
Villous blunting and epithelial injury reduce small-intestinal absorptive function, producing malabsorption.
Mucosal epithelial injury in adult AIE manifests as secretory diarrhea.
Debilitating diarrhea and malabsorption downstream of mucosal injury can produce weight loss.
Secretory diarrheal losses can produce electrolyte disturbances including hypokalemia.
